title: International Classification of Sleep Disorders, Third Edition
authority: classification source subject to ICSD-3-TR updates
apaReference: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
revisionReference: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
revisionPolicy: ICSD-3-TR nomenclature and criteria changes override older ICSD-3 wording when a conflict exists.
copyrightBoundary: Glossary term names are inventoried. Learner definitions and memory clues are original Sleep Pathways Guild summaries rather than reproduced ICSD glossary prose.

items.definition: A disorder in which excessive sleepiness is a defining clinical feature.
items.memoryClue: Hypersomnia is a disorder; hypersomnolence is the symptom state.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Vivid dreamlike perceptions that occur while transitioning from wakefulness into sleep.
items.memoryClue: Hypnagogic = going into sleep.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Vivid dreamlike perceptions that occur while transitioning from sleep to wakefulness.
items.memoryClue: Hypnopompic = coming out of sleep.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Muscle pain.
items.memoryClue: Myalgia simply means muscle pain.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Sleep perceived as unrefreshing or poor in quality despite having had an opportunity to sleep.
items.memoryClue: The person sleeps but does not feel restored.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A statistical measure comparing the odds of an outcome in one group with the odds in another group.
items.memoryClue: Odds ratio compares odds between groups.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Dream-enactment behavior, usually arising from REM sleep.
items.memoryClue: Oneirism refers to acting out dream content.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Sleep testing performed outside a sleep center, usually with fewer physiologic channels than in-laboratory polysomnography.
items.memoryClue: Out-of-center testing usually means limited-channel home testing.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An accidental fatal event arising from complex parasomnia behavior that may be mistaken for intentional self-harm.
items.memoryClue: The behavior occurs from parasomnia, not suicidal intent.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A neurodegenerative movement disorder characterized by features such as bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor, or postural instability.
items.memoryClue: Parkinson disease can affect both movement and sleep.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A shift of circadian timing earlier or later relative to its prior position.
items.memoryClue: Advance = earlier; delay = later.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A graph showing how the direction and size of a circadian phase shift depend on when a time cue is given.
items.memoryClue: Timing of light or another cue determines advance versus delay.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The ability to remain asleep or awake at a circadian phase that is biologically unfavorable for that state.
items.memoryClue: Phase tolerance is coping with the 'wrong' biological time.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A persistent state of increased physiologic activation associated with insomnia and measurable in autonomic, metabolic, or sleep-latency findings.
items.memoryClue: Hyperarousal can keep the body in a wake-promoting state.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A gene in which pathogenic variants are strongly associated with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.
items.memoryClue: PHOX2B is the key gene associated with congenital central hypoventilation.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The proportion of a population that has a disease or condition at a specified time or over a specified period.
items.memoryClue: Prevalence asks how common a condition is.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.term: REM Sleep without Atonia, REM-without Atonia
items.definition: Loss or reduction of the normal muscle atonia expected during REM sleep, seen as excessive tonic or phasic muscle activity.
items.memoryClue: REM normally has atonia; RSWA means that atonia is reduced.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A tendency for a person to sleep better than usual during the first night in a sleep laboratory.
items.memoryClue: Reverse first-night effect means first-night sleep improves instead of worsens.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Episodes of falling asleep inappropriately with little or no warning.
items.memoryClue: Sleep attacks can occur with minimal warning.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A daily record of sleep timing, duration, quality, and related behaviors kept over multiple days or weeks.
items.memoryClue: A sleep diary records the pattern night by night.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Prolonged difficulty becoming fully alert after awakening, often with confusion, repeated returns to sleep, or automatic behavior.
items.memoryClue: Sleep drunkenness is prolonged, impaired awakening.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The sleep-regulating process in which pressure for sleep builds with time awake and is reduced by sleep.
items.memoryClue: Longer wakefulness increases homeostatic sleep pressure.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Behaviors and environmental practices intended to support adequate, regular, and good-quality sleep.
items.memoryClue: Sleep hygiene addresses habits and environment.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A REM period occurring within 15 minutes of sleep onset during an MSLT nap or overnight PSG.
items.memoryClue: SOREMP = REM very soon after sleep begins.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Sexualized behaviors that arise from sleep, most often from NREM sleep, as a form of parasomnia.
items.memoryClue: The behavior originates from sleep.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Violent behavior arising from sleep in association with a parasomnia, often after accidental provocation of the sleeper.
items.memoryClue: The violence is parasomnia-related rather than planned waking behavior.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A controlled test performed during quiet wakefulness to evaluate leg-movement activity and sensory symptoms associated with restless legs syndrome.
items.memoryClue: The patient remains still while leg activity and symptoms are assessed.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
